title: Security Management Process
text: Implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations. Minimum requirements include: risk analysis (accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI held by the covered entity), risk management, sanction policy, and information system activity review.

title: Assigned Security Responsibility
text: Identify the security official who is responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by the Security Rule.

title: Workforce Security
text: Implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of the workforce have appropriate access to ePHI and to prevent those who do not have access under the policies from obtaining access. Includes authorization and/or supervision, workforce clearance procedures, and termination procedures.

title: Information Access Management
text: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to ePHI, consistent with the Privacy Rule, including access authorization, access establishment and modification (isolation of health care clearinghouse functions), and access control procedures.

title: Security Awareness and Training
text: Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of the workforce (including management). Includes security reminders, protection from malicious software, log-in monitoring, and password management procedures.

title: Security Incident Procedures
text: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents: identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate, to the extent practicable, harmful effects; document security incidents and their outcomes; and periodically review incident records.

title: Contingency Plan
text: Establish and implement policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or disaster that damages systems containing ePHI, including: data backup plan, disaster recovery plan, emergency mode operation plan, testing and revision procedures, and applications and data criticality analysis.

title: Evaluation
text: Perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, in response to environmental or operational changes, of how well the entity's policies and procedures meet the requirements of the Security Rule.

title: Business Associate Contracts
text: Obtain satisfactory assurances, in the form of a contract or other arrangement, that business associates will appropriately safeguard the ePHI they access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit on behalf of the covered entity.

title: Facility Access Controls
text: Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems (and facilities where they are housed) to authorized persons only, including: contingency operations, facility security plan, access control and validation procedures, and maintenance records.

title: Workstation Use
text: Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed and the manner in which those functions are performed by workstations and any other electronic devices that access ePHI.

title: Workstation Security
text: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access ePHI to restrict access to authorized users. Workstations must not be left unattended in a way that exposes ePHI.

title: Device and Media Controls
text: Implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing ePHI into and out of a facility, and the movement of such items within the facility: disposal, media re-use, accountability, and data backup and storage.

title: Access Control
text: Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain ePHI to allow access only to persons or software programs granted access rights, including: unique user identification, emergency access procedures, automatic logoff, and encryption and decryption.

title: Audit Controls
text: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use ePHI, including audit logs of user activity and access.

title: Integrity Controls
text: Implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction, including a mechanism to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.

title: Person or Entity Authentication
text: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.

title: Transmission Security
text: Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI transmitted over an electronic communications network, with integrity controls to ensure ePHI is not improperly modified without detection (during transmission) and appropriately encrypting ePHI whenever deemed appropriate.

title: Organizational Requirements
text: Covered entities must enter into HIPAA-compliant business associate agreements, and apply the Security Rule requirements to their business associates, including ensuring BA agreements contain satisfactory assurances for both the covered entity and any subcontractors.

title: Policies and Procedures and Documentation Requirements
text: Adopt reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the Security Rule, maintain written documentation of such policies, procedures, actions, and assessments, retain the documentation for at least six years, and review/update it in response to environmental or operational changes.
